stages.title: Source
stages.what: Where the data comes from: a versioned store, recorded sweeps or a folder of your own. A source has no input and carries a data card.

stages.title: Prepare
stages.what: What is done to the samples before any network: a licence recipe, a choice of samples, crops, normalising, denoising, segmenting, rendering, a realism edit.

stages.title: Split
stages.what: Which person goes to train, validation or test. Persons are split, never scans, so no person is on two sides.

stages.title: Augment
stages.what: Random changes to the training samples only, drawn afresh each epoch.

stages.title: Model
stages.what: The network, built from the type of the data it takes: its stem from the channels and rank, its head from the classes.

stages.title: Train
stages.what: Fits the model on the train part while watching the validation part, and gives a checkpoint.

stages.title: Calibrate
stages.what: Fits how sure a trained model is on the validation part, never on test.

stages.title: Select
stages.what: Joins the arms of a screen and keeps one by its validation score alone.

stages.title: Evaluate
stages.what: Reads the held-out test part once and gives numbers with intervals, or measures speed or distance between data sets.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.what: Measures or names what the data holds with no network trained: morphometry, naming by rule.

stages.title: Report
stages.what: Writes down what a run did and found: the CLAIM and REFORMS report, the model card, the W&B log.

kinds.data: samples with their axes, sizes, labels, split parts and person key
kinds.model: a network not yet trained, shaped by the type of the data it was built for
kinds.checkpoint: a trained network's weights, with the record of the data it was trained on
kinds.metrics: numbers measured on data or on a checkpoint, each with its interval where it has one
kinds.report: a written record of a run: a report, a model card or a log

requirements.title: Identity
requirements.rule: The manifest says block 1; its id is 2 to 40 lower-case letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter, and is the file's name; its version is a whole number from 1; it has a title of 1 to 60 characters, a stage from the list, a one-line summary of at most 120 characters, what it does in at most 800, and a glyph from the list.

requirements.title: Ports
requirements.rule: A source has no input and every other block at least one; every block has at least one output. Port names are unique. Each input says what it accepts as a pattern; each output says which input it starts from and the ops that change the type; every op is known and every reference names a param or port that exists.

requirements.title: Params
requirements.rule: Each param is a choice, an int, a float, a bool, a set or a list of names, with valid bounds and a default inside them; names are unique; a float has at most 6 decimals.

requirements.title: Rules
requirements.rule: Each rule names params that exist in its when and its need, uses only the conditions in, not_in, min, max, above, below, empty and nonempty, and says in words what is wrong when it fails.

requirements.title: Reads
requirements.rule: The block lists the split parts it reads; only an evaluate or a report block may read the test part.

requirements.title: Job
requirements.rule: The job's class is none, cpu or gpu; its hours are above 0 or a reference to a number param; it asks for 1 to 64 CPUs and 1 to 512 GB; it says whether it rides in its upstream's job and whether its arms go as one array.

requirements.title: Determinism
requirements.rule: The block is exact (the same inputs give the same bytes), seeded by a named int param, or declared, saying what varies and why that is tolerated.

requirements.title: Genericity
requirements.rule: A block that takes data or a model says which ranks, time axis, channels and sizes it takes, and why, with what would widen it, where it takes less than all; each data input's rank is that rank; and it accepts every probe of its ranks and time, given the targets and the split its first input asks for, and computes its outputs from it with no problem.

requirements.title: Needs
requirements.rule: The libraries the block uses come only from the contract's list.

requirements.title: Code
requirements.rule: existing: every path the block names exists in the repository; own: tools/sandbox/blocks/<id>.py with a module docstring and def run(inputs, params, context), and tests/test_sandbox_block_<id>.py; planned: no code on this branch yet, its today planned, or pending while an unmerged pull request builds it.

requirements.title: Today
requirements.rule: The block says truly what runs it now: live (the experiment route), a gate word with a fixed id, a launched flow's fixed plan, an unmerged pull request named by #number, or planned (nothing yet).

requirements.title: Text
requirements.rule: Every string is ASCII with no control character, and the manifest's canonical JSON is at most 16384 bytes.

requirements.title: Data card
requirements.rule: A source block fills every field of its data card (origin, where, count, persons, split, held out, licence) and lists the repository files its facts come from.
